about: Vectors for the x402 batch-settlement pairings (the x402-batch-settlement entry point of @integraledger/lcp). H is SHA-256("abc") and H' SHA-256("abd"); EVM keys are the published Anvil development accounts 0, 1 and 3, and EB10's refund authorizer account 2's address; the EVM values were computed with eth-account 0.14.0, eth-abi 6.0.0, eth-utils 6.0.0 and viem 2.57.4 and read them on Base Sepolia; the SVM values with solders 0.26.0, PyNaCl 1.6.2 and @noble/curves 2.4.0. The SVM fixtures (ES4's top_up, request_close and nonce-memo wires, ES5's landed wire, the no-channel transaction) were built with solders 0.26.0 on Python 3.11; the same script reproduces ES1, ES2, ES3 and ES5's txid. The receiver authorizer is the key of seed 03x32. An SVM opening carries two Memo instructions, the seller memo (extra.memo, L) and then x402's receiver-authorizer binding memo, whose UTF-8 data is x402:batch-settlement:svm:rcvauth:v1: and the base58 key (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/schemes/batch-settlement/scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L121-127 and L1320-1325; the order is the steward SDK's, typescript/packages/mechanisms/svm/src/payment-channels/open.ts:464-467, and the text its batch-settlement/receiverBinding.ts:19 and test/unit/batch.receiverAuthorizer.test.ts, "round-trips the binding memo and rejects anything else", at the same commit). ES5 is a landed opening read by recover, landedErr the error it is read landed with; transactionV1's statusRows read the stock version-1 opening back, and the read's own cases are in svm-read.json. EB7's laterDeposit, laterDepositByPayer and plantOtherContract, each a transaction that is not this deposit, answer pending search-incomplete: the read defines no search for H, and at coverage full failed comes only from a search read whole (read-status rule 24). EB10 is the scheme's refund-authorizer mode, its values from the stock @x402/evm 2.31.0 client as its case states. transactionV1 is the version-1 transaction (SIMD-0385) the stock @x402/svm 2.31.0 client writes, run offline as its case states; its landed wire adds the fee payer's signature made with @noble/curves 2.4.0.

evm.channelConfigType: ChannelConfig(address payer,address payerAuthorizer,address receiver,address receiverAuthorizer,address token,uint40 withdrawDelay,bytes32 salt)

EB3.case: the opening's ERC-3009 deposit. expectPayload is complete's payment for the payer's signature (signature) and the payer authorizer's voucher signature (EB2.signature), written by hand from x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/schemes/batch-settlement/scheme_batch_settlement_evm.md L118-164 (payload type "deposit", channelConfig, voucher {channelId, maxClaimableAmount, signature}, deposit {amount, authorization {erc3009Authorization {validAfter "0", validBefore, salt, signature}}}) with fixed.evm's config, deposit, validBefore and authSalt, wrapped in x402 v2's PaymentPayload (specs/x402-specification-v2.md §5.2.1: x402Version, resource, accepted, payload, then extensions, the document's own, echoed); Python 3.12.3's json.dumps of the object, compact, is its JSON text.

EB4.case: the opening's Permit2 deposit, the option's extra with assetTransferMethod "permit2". signature is eth-keys 0.8.0's deterministic (RFC 6979) signature of digest with fixed.evm.payerKey. expectPayload is complete's payment for that signature and EB2.signature, written by hand from x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/schemes/batch-settlement/scheme_batch_settlement_evm.md L114-116 (exactly one of erc3009Authorization and permit2Authorization) and the steward SDK's Permit2 deposit (the same commit, typescript/packages/mechanisms/evm/src/batch-settlement/client/permit2.ts L37-50 and L77-90: permit2Authorization {from, permitted {token, amount}, spender the Permit2 deposit collector, nonce, deadline, witness {channelId}, signature}), wrapped in x402 v2's PaymentPayload (specs/x402-specification-v2.md §5.2.1: x402Version, resource, accepted, payload, then extensions, the document's own, echoed); Python 3.12.3's json.dumps of the object, compact, is its JSON text.

plant.case: a voucher payload whose voucher.channelId is EB1 but whose channelConfig.salt is H'

EB6.case: bound and the channel members. expectVoucherPayload and expectRefundPayload are buildWithin's completes for fixed.evm.config at maxClaimableAmount 1000 with EB2.signature, without and with refund {amount refundAmount}, written by hand from x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/schemes/batch-settlement/scheme_batch_settlement_evm.md L166-190 (type "voucher", channelConfig, voucher) and L192-221 (type "refund", channelConfig, voucher, amount), wrapped in x402 v2's PaymentPayload (specs/x402-specification-v2.md §5.2.1: x402Version, resource, accepted, payload, then extensions, the document's own, echoed); Python 3.12.3's json.dumps of the object, compact, is its JSON text.

EB7.case: status from what landed, with EB3's reference naming the transaction 0xab..ab, on fixture receipts (finalized 100, safe 105); the token's authorizationState for the payer and EB3's deposit nonce reads true from block reader.used where the receipt uses the nonce. The opening is the channel contract's Deposited for EB1's channel in a transaction that consumed the deposit authorization's nonce (USDC's AuthorizationUsed for the payer and that nonce); what moved is the deposit's amount to the channel's receiver, by its Deposited log; a Deposited for the channel with no use of the nonce is a later deposit, an act of another kind; a Deposited from another contract is no act. The reader answers no block and no logs, so no search reads to a head and none is whole

fullCall.case: the deposit call as the ERC-3009 collector makes it: USDC's AuthorizationUsed for the payer's deposit authorization (EB3's deposit nonce), the payer's transfer to the collector, the collector's to the channel contract, ChannelCreated (EB8's log) and Deposited with its amount and the channel's new balance

laterDeposit.case: the full call's Deposited alone, with no use of the deposit nonce and no transfer of the payer's, and the nonce unused: a later deposit into the channel that names no signer, since the channel contract's deposit takes any non-zero collector and checks only that its own balance rose by the amount (x402-foundation/x402 f8f83309, contracts/evm/src/x402BatchSettlement.sol L200-231); a foreign item under another account's signature; the value unused, the search not whole

laterDepositByPayer.case: the full call's Deposited with the payer's Transfer of its amount to the ERC-3009 deposit collector before it, no use of the deposit nonce, and the nonce unused: a later deposit into the channel by the payer's own act, the collector moving only what the payer signed, a foreign item of another kind; the value unused, the search not whole

plantOtherContract.case: a Deposited for EB1's channel from another contract than the channel contract: no act; the nonce unused

EB9.case: batchEvm.buildWithin over the EB1 channel (fixed.evm.config) with EB2's maxClaimableAmount, its one request completed with EB2's signature: refund absent is a voucher, refund given (an object, or null) is a refund, with amount only when refund.amount is a decimal amount; refund.amount present and not an amount is refused.

refund {amount: 400}

EB10.case: the scheme's refund-authorizer mode, which the stock @x402/evm 2.31.0 client marks by extra.voucherManager "facilitator" and a non-zero extra.refundAuthorizer (dist/esm/chunk-AEYKXGQA.mjs:232-250, buildChannelConfig) and the stock server announces (dist/esm/batch-settlement/server/index.mjs:2412-2423). The channel salt is the stock client's packing, the entropy's first 12 bytes, or its last 12 where those are zero, then the refund authorizer's 20 bytes (packRefundAuthorizerSalt, dist/esm/chunk-7DJ4WEQ5.mjs:218-223); H is the deposit authorization's salt, from which the ERC-3009 nonce is keccak256(abi.encode(channelId, salt)) (buildErc3009DepositNonce, dist/esm/chunk-W6ON4LG2.mjs:3-7), or the deposit permit's nonce. refundAuthorizer is Anvil development account 2. Each packing row's expectChannelConfig and expectChannelId are the stock client's buildChannelConfig and computeChannelId for fixed.evm's payer and payer authorizer, the row's entropy as the client's salt and this option, and expectDepositNonce viem 2.57's keccak256 of that encoding for H. Each method's expectPayload is lcp's complete for fixed.evm's choice with authSalt the first row's entropy, signed with fixed.evm's keys (viem's deterministic signatures; digest is viem's hashTypedData of the deposit authorization); input is viem's encodeFunctionData of the stock batchSettlementABI's deposit with that config, the deposit's amount, the method's deposit collector and the collector data the stock facilitator encodes (buildErc3009CollectorData and buildPermit2CollectorData, dist/esm/chunk-W6ON4LG2.mjs:8-31); receipt holds the logs the channel contract and its collectors emit for that call (the token's AuthorizationUsed and Transfers on ERC-3009, Permit2's Transfer from the payer to the channel contract, ChannelCreated and Deposited), encoded with viem's encodeEventTopics; expectStatus and expectRecover are what lcp's read gives for them, the transaction named by transaction, read with reader's marks, the token's authorizationState, or the payer's Permit2 bit, reading used from block reader.used

eip3009.case: the ERC-3009 deposit: erc3009Authorization.salt is H

permit2.case: the Permit2 deposit: the permit's nonce is H, in decimal

ES2.case: ES2's opening. messageLength, messageSha256 and the wire (wireBase64, wireLength, wireSha256Prefix) are of the message as solders 0.26.0 compiles it, the account keys of each class in byte order. build compiles the same instructions with its account keys in @solana/kit's order, the order of the steward SDK, which compiles its open transaction with @solana/kit (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, typescript/packages/mechanisms/svm/src/payment-channels/open.ts L501-516); buildMessageSha256 is the SHA-256 of that message, computed with @solana/kit 8.4.0 as getCompiledTransactionMessageEncoder of compileTransactionMessage of ES2's message decompiled, and node:crypto's SHA-256. lcp compiles with the same @solana/kit, so the value is independent of lcp in its input, solders' message, and not in its compiler. buildWireSha256 is the SHA-256 of the wire complete writes for the payer's signature over that message, written by hand from the Solana transaction format: the compact-u16 count of required signatures, one 64-byte slot per required signer, zero but for the payer's, which holds the payer's Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032) of the message with fixed.svm.payerSeed, then the message. It is computed in Python 3.12.3 without @solana/kit: the message compiled by hand in @solana/kit's account order (the fee payer; then signers before non-signers and writable before read-only; then the base58 text as Intl.Collator("en", {caseFirst: "lower"}) orders it) from the solders wire, giving buildMessageSha256; the signature with cryptography 50.0.1's Ed25519, and the hash with hashlib.

plantSalt43.case: a voucher payload whose voucher.channelId is ES1 and whose channelConfig.salt is 43

ES6.case: a full refund: buildWithin with refund {} carries the voucher for maxClaimableAmount, the server's accepted cumulative amount, with expiresAt 0, and no amount; with recentBlockhash it also carries a payer-signed request_close, which x402 sends only on a retry after invalid_batch_settlement_svm_receiver_binding_unavailable (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L626-636; the steward SDK's typescript/packages/mechanisms/svm/src/batch-settlement/client/channel.ts:281-312, and test/unit/batch.refund.test.ts, "resends with a request_close when the facilitator has no binding", at the same commit). The request_close is the Compute Budget prefix (limit 200000, price 1 microlamport), request_close (data 05) of the payment-channels program with exactly the payer (read-only signer) and the channel PDA (writable), then one Memo v3 with extra.memo when the option carries one, else none; fee payer extra.feePayer.

It is computed in Python 3.12.3 without @solana/kit: the message compiled by hand in @solana/kit's account order (the fee payer; then signers before non-signers and writable before read-only; then the base58 text as Intl.Collator("en", {caseFirst: "lower"}) orders it) from the solders wire, giving buildMessageSha256; the signature with cryptography 50.0.1's Ed25519, and the hash with hashlib.

loneSurrogateMemo.case: the retry, with ES4's option whose extra.memo holds a lone surrogate (U+D800): a string with no UTF-8 form (The Unicode Standard 16.0, section 3.9, D92: UTF-8 encodes no surrogate code point; Python 3's str.encode('utf-8') raises UnicodeEncodeError for it), so the request_close's memo cannot carry the bytes the caller gave, and nothing is built

ES8.case: the opening's memos: exactly one receiver-authorizer binding memo and exactly one other Memo instruction, in either order, the other carrying H; any other count is refused (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L1320-1325 and L1346-1348: the open suffix carries exactly one binding Memo and the facilitator requires exactly one Memo besides it; the steward SDK's payment-channels/open.ts:1199-1224 and test/unit/batch.receiverAuthorizer.test.ts, "requires exactly one matching binding memo in the open", which rejects an open with no binding memo and one with two). Each wire is ES2's opening with only its memos changed, built with solders 0.26.0 and signed by the payer; bound reads it as deposit.transaction under ES4's option and config, and recover reads it landed.

L alone

ES9.case: pairingOf and advertise of fixed.svm.option, whose extra.withdrawDelay is 3600, with maxTimeoutSeconds replaced by each row's value. x402 751590a2, scheme_batch_settlement_svm.md L235 and L247: maxTimeoutSeconds is a number, and withdrawDelay MUST be >= maxTimeoutSeconds. That comparison is read only when maxTimeoutSeconds is a JSON number, never by converting a string or an array to one; an option whose maxTimeoutSeconds is of another type is not one the pairing's filter serves, because its timeout is not a positive safe integer: advertise and build refuse it, and pairingOf names no pairing for it. A row without maxTimeoutSeconds removes the member. expectAdvertise null: the option is advertised.

ES10.case: The point rule a PDA candidate meets: 32 bytes are a point when ed25519.Point.fromBytes(bytes, true) of @noble/curves 2.4.0 accepts them, decompression only: y is the little-endian integer with bit 255 cleared, taken modulo p = 2^255 - 19, and x^2 = (y^2 - 1) / (d y^2 + 1) must have a square root, so x = 0 with the sign bit set decodes. Each row's point value is Python 3's integer arithmetic (Euler's criterion), and noble agrees.

y = p + 1, which is 1 modulo p, with the sign bit set

EC1.case: the Cloudflare payment. payload is the decoded PAYMENT-SIGNATURE of x402's batch-settlement Cloudflare scheme (x402-foundation/x402 751590a2, specs/schemes/batch-settlement/scheme_batch_settlement_cloudflare.md L143-160: x402Version, payload {amount, asset}, accepted), with the extensions echoed at the top level (L168-170), written by hand; payloadLength is the length of its compact JSON text. build writes the same members in the same order from the chosen option, its extensions the document's.

transactionV1.case: A version-1 transaction as the stock client writes it: @x402/svm 2.31.0 (npm, the devDependency this package pins), run offline: the payer's key from Ed25519 seed 01x32 (@solana/kit 8.4.0 createKeyPairSignerFromPrivateKeyBytes), the clock at now, the option's extra.recentBlockhash as the lifetime and transactionVersions [0, 1] as a stock facilitator advertises them (scheme_exact_svm.md §1.5 at x402-foundation/x402 88b66dd4), so the client builds version 1, the highest version both sides admit; the client's one RPC read, getAccountInfo of the asset, answered with an initialized SPL Token mint of 6 decimals owned by the Token program, and no other read made, the client configured with fixed.svm's salt and deposit and no channel discovery, so its first payload is the deposit that opens fixed.svm.config's channel. bound gives H from the one memo, extra.memo; reference gives the message's digest, the fee payer and the blockhash. landedWireBase64 is the stock wire with the fee payer's Ed25519 signature (seed 02x32, @noble/curves 2.4.0) of the message in signature slot 0; txid is that signature in base58. The message is every byte before the signatures (SIMD-0385, Transaction V1 Specification, at solana-foundation/solana-improvement-documents ae7b00f3), and messageSha256 is SHA-256 over it (node:crypto). status of the landed wire's reference, its transaction the txid, read back through a constructed reader (the buyer's account listing the txid with its memo as getSignaturesForAddress renders it; getTransaction holding it at finalized, or at confirmed alone, with the token balances getTransaction gives for each token account its TransferChecked names, the source the payer's and the destination the payee's; the finalized slot 1,100, the confirmed one 1,120; the blockhash valid at slot 1,000), answers each row's expect at the one mark, finalized (read-status rules 13, 17, 23 to 25): settled, with what moved and presented yes; pending, below-mark, naming it with no finality, where only confirmed holds it; and, with an error, pending, search-incomplete, since the search's gate holds the payer's own failed transaction while the search proves no absence. recover gives H. changed holds the stock wire with one member changed, each refused by bound with its code; landedChanged is the landed wire with the memo changed as changed's first row, read under the same txid, which status answers pending, instrument-live, since its message digest is not the reference's, so it consumed nothing and is no act carrying H, and the blockhash's validity has not passed

statusRows.case: the landed wire at finalized: settled, what moved named by its transaction and place, presented yes
the landed wire at confirmed alone, the latest head and no mark: pending, below-mark, naming it with no finality
the landed wire at finalized with an error, the payer's own failed transaction: the search's gate holds it, pending, search-incomplete

changed.case: the memo's last character, d, changed to e inside the signed message: the memo carries another hash than extra.memo's
the version byte 129 changed to 130, a message version SIMD-0385 does not define
one byte appended after the signatures, where SIMD-0385 admits none

landedChanged.case: the landed wire with its memo changed, under the same txid: no act carrying H and not the message presented, so the value reads unconsumed: pending, instrument-live

build.case: lcp's build of the same inputs the stock client was given, under presented.accepted offered alone in a document: its extra.transactionVersions holds 1, so it builds version 1, and the message it asks the payer to sign is the stock client's message byte for byte, every byte of presented's wire before the signatures as @solana/kit 8.4.0's getTransactionDecoder reads messageBytes. input is the choice beside the document and option; a bigint member is written in decimal. The payer authorizer is the payer, the salt, open slot and deposit the stock client's (fixed.svm), and the compute budget build's default, 200000 units at 1 micro-lamport, the stock open's OPEN_DEFAULT_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT and DEFAULT_COMPUTE_UNIT_PRICE_MICROLAMPORTS (dist/esm/chunk-DP3B4MQJ.mjs:931; chunk-DAIKIZVB.mjs:13).

transactionVersions.case: build of ES2's opening input, and buildWithin of ES6.withMemo's refund with recentBlockhash (refundRows), each under ES4's option with extra.transactionVersions set to each row's value, or without it for the row that has none, both in the document and as the chosen option. scheme_exact_svm.md §1.5 at x402-foundation/x402 88b66dd4: extra.transactionVersions holds the transaction message versions the sponsor accepts, the JSON integers 0 and 1; when it is absent the accepted set is [0]; a field holding any other entry is invalid; @x402/svm 2.31.0's resolveTransactionVersion (dist/esm/chunk-DAIKIZVB.mjs:289-309) builds the highest version both admit and refuses a value that is not an array, an entry other than 0 and 1, and an empty list. The rule: the client builds as the stock clients do, the highest version both the offer's list and this package admit, version 1 where the list holds 1, version 0 where it holds 0 alone or is absent; an offer whose list admits neither, a field that is present and is not a non-empty array of the integers 0 and 1, is refused at the option filter, before the buyer signs. A row whose field holds 1 is built as version 1, its first byte 129: the opening's SHA-256 is transactionV1.messageSha256, the opening @x402/svm 2.31.0's batch-settlement client writes for the same inputs (transactionV1); the request_close's is that of the message @solana/kit 8.4.0 alone writes from ES4.closeWireBase64's instructions without its Compute Budget instructions, the same fee payer and blockhash, and the header buildWithin's default budget gives as @x402/svm 2.31.0's applyTransactionV1Config writes one (dist/esm/chunk-RZ6M7L3U.mjs:40-53): computeUnitLimit 200000, priorityFeeLamports 1 (200000 units at 1 micro-lamport, rounded up), loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit 4194304 (test/kit-v1.ts). A row whose field holds 0 alone, or that has none, is built as the file's version-0 message, its first byte 128 and its SHA-256 the build's buildMessageSha256 as the input's own vector records it (ES2.buildMessageSha256; ES6.withMemo.buildMessageSha256); any other row is refused x402/option-malformed by the option filter, with no request to sign. A refund without recentBlockhash builds no transaction and carries the voucher alone under every row the filter admits.

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes the batch-settlement specification leaves to the implementation. A row with pairing and call runs that pairing's function: with choice, call(choice, H); with h, build of ES2's choice, the advertised Solana option with the svm payer as payer and payerAuthorizer, deposit, salt 42, openSlot, tokenProgram and blockhash as recentBlockhash, with that h; with zeroMembers, the EVM build of EB2 and EB3's opening once per member named, with that member the zero address: from in its choice, or payTo or asset in fixed.evm.option. A row with pairing and calls runs each of those functions of that pairing on an opening. On the EVM pairing it is EB2 and EB3's opening: the EVM build of fixed.evm.option advertised under H, with the payer, payer authorizer, deposit, authSalt and now of fixed.evm, completed with EB3's and EB2's signatures, and the same build for a Permit2 deposit (the option's extra.assetTransferMethod permit2), completed with the same signatures, which no read verifies; buildWithin takes the advertised option and EB2's maxClaimableAmount. On the Solana pairing it is ES2's opening as ES4 presents it: ES4's config, a voucher for ES1's PDA, and ES2's wire as deposit.transaction; buildWithin takes the advertised Solana option and maxClaimableAmount 1000. With depositAmount, deposit.amount is replaced by it. With validBeforeOrDeadline, the ERC-3009 authorization's validBefore, or the Permit2 authorization's deadline, is replaced by it. With configMembers, each member set replaces those members of channelConfig, one run per set; voucher.channelId is the channel id of the configuration that results, and buildWithin takes that configuration, under H. With refundAmounts, each value is the amount of a refund payload that carries the opening's channelConfig and voucher, one run per value.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.
